newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH says Guinness sale generated capital gain.
newsitem.headline: LVMH says Guinness sale generated capital gain.

text.p: French luxury goods group LVMH said on Friday that it sold a seven percent stake in Guinness Plc at a higher price than it paid for the shares.
"We sold the shares at a higher price than we bought them," a spokeswoman for LVMH told Reuters, but would not elaborate.
One analyst estimated the capital gain at over one billion francs but said the exchange rate made an exact calculation difficult.

Analysts said LVMH's decision to cut its stake in Guinness to 14 percent from 21 percent and focus on luxury goods augurs well for its profitability in the long-term. But they said it was difficult to calculate the short-term impact.
Another analyst said a technical change in the way the smaller Guinness stake will contribute to LVMH's 1997 accounts may have a negative impact of 220 million francs this year on earnings.
Because the stake has fallen below 20 percent, it would be accounted on a cost basis and no longer on an equity consolidated basis, analysts said.

That means the contribution to LVMH results would depend on the dividend stream as opposed to being a percentage of Guinness's book value, as it was when LVMH's stake in Guinness was greater than 20 percent.
The company had no immediate comment on the impact of the stake sale on 1997 results.
